name: Jotham
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: Ahaz son of Jotham begins to reign over Judah and does not that which is right, but walks in the way of the kings of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: The record was reckoned by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel, keeping the account by name.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: The rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet wrote. Uzziah slept with his fathers and they buried him in the field of burial that belonged to the kings, for they said, He is a leper. Jotham his son reigned in his stead.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

points: Jotham was twenty and five years old when he began to reign and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High, according to all that his father Uzziah did, only he did not enter into the temple of the Most High. He would not go into the temple, and the people still did corruptly.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 27: Jotham Becomes Mighty Because He Prepared His Ways

points: Jotham became mighty because he prepared his ways before the Most High. It is a short chapter, but the point is plain: the Most High was with our forefathers when they followed the commandments, and Jotham ordered his ways before God.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 27: Jotham Becomes Mighty Because He Prepared His Ways

points: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerns Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. These are the days in which Isaiah prophesied.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: In the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up toward Jerusalem to war, but could not prevail against it.

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

points: The word of the Lord came unto Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

note.label: Hosea 1: A Wife of Whoredoms and the Sand of the Sea

points: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

note.label: Micah 1: The Lord Cometh Forth Out of His Place
